decisions.executionNote: Approach basket with left arm, raising wrist while turning gripper downward. Target board appears to show a yellow/red snack cup; basket grasp geometry remains uncertain.

Hold left at its reachable staging pose; advance right fingers along basket right wall with small downward-orientation correction.
Move right fingers slightly forward across the basket side lip, close, then make a small test lift. Verify actual retention in images.
Retract right arm while lifting the closed basket grasp, avoiding the forward reach limit; watch basket motion to establish retention.
Reduce retract-and-lift increments near the right-arm kinematic boundary. Keep basket gripper fully closed.
Lift basket farther while retracting to safe reach; align left open grasp with the yellow/red cup, accounting for wrist-to-finger offset.
Basket did not visibly follow the lift; reopen right and reapproach rim with a shallower wrist angle. Left tracks cup without grasping yet.
Shift right grasp outward to straddle basket sidewall rather than its interior, close and make a small test lift. Left tracks target lid.
Allow basket grasp to finish closing, then raise and retract right hand to check whether the basket is retained above the conveyor.
Basket again appears unretained. Reopen and approach farther right and forward to straddle its actual near-right rim; maintain left tracking of target.
Replan from interrupted pose: descend with smaller lateral motion and a shallower approach to reach basket lip, keeping elbow configuration continuous.
Downward contact suggests one finger is on the lip. Shift outward across the basket right side and close without pressing farther down.
Test the rim grasp by lifting and retracting gently, with closed right gripper. Continue tracking the cup with the open left hand.
Secure the image-matching cup before it leaves left workspace. Reorient right gripper to grasp basket front lip across its thickness instead of chasing the side.
Finish cup closure and gently test retention. Use smaller yaw increments to align right jaws across basket front wall, lower below lip, and close.
Cup was not retained; reopen and catch its body at the left workspace boundary. Hold right rim closure, then test lift with reduced reach.
Center cup between left fingers before closing, using a shallower approach for reach margin. Reopen right and undo excess yaw that displaced fingers left of basket.
Adjust left fingertip offset toward the cup without crossing wrists; recenter and close. Right approaches accessible basket left-side rim by reducing yaw and advancing slightly.
Test cup retention with a lift back into left workspace. Move right fingers across the basket's near corner and close, staying away from full extension.
Cup was not retained. Clear left arm. Lower open right fingers farther below the basket lip before closing, correcting likely excessive grasp height.
Basket remains beyond the fingertips. Use a shallower wrist angle to extend fingers forward while lowering the wrist, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Correct the forward offset: basket sidewall is farther along the belt than the previous fingertip placement. Advance right fingers to the left wall and close.
Avoid the forward IK boundary by lowering the wrist and flattening the approach, letting fingertip offset reach farther toward the basket wall.
Basket wall is visible to the right of the fingers. Angle the shallow right grasp outward to reach the wall with limited wrist translation, then close.
Basket is moving beyond safe right-arm reach and the grasp is empty. Retract to maintain reach margin and approach the matching cup now in right workspace.
Retry retraction at half scale after zero-step joint-continuity rejection; preserve current elbow configuration.
Bring right open gripper over the yellow/red cup, raising the wrist and rotating toward a downward grasp while staying in right workspace.
Align open right fingers around the cup body below its lid, correcting the forward offset seen in earlier missed grasps.
The open finger displaced the cup left. Lift slightly to clear the lid, recenter over its observed body, then lower and close.
Cup is now tipped and previous fingers were too high. Reopen, track its body, descend about five centimeters, and close around the lower body.
Finish closing on the lowered cup grasp, then lift and retract slightly to test actual retention.
Cup remained on the belt, offset right and below the closed jaws. Reopen, shift right with conveyor motion, and descend to the body's actual height before closing.
Continue following the moving cup while closure completes, correcting a small remaining lateral offset, then test a short lift.
Correct grasp depth: the cup was near finger ends but below the closing pads. Reopen, advance slightly, and lower the pads around the cup body before closing.
Allow the deeper grasp to close fully and lift seven centimeters, checking whether the cup actually follows rather than relying on gripper state.
Cup is still unretained and farther right than the jaws. Clear it while open, move over the observed low tilted body, then descend around it.
Replan with smaller lateral increments after the guard interruption. Lower the open pads around the tilted cup, then close while matching its motion.
Cup remains offset to the right of the closing fingers. Reopen briefly and move the low grasp laterally and slightly forward onto its body, then close.
Reduce translation near the reach boundary. Adjust wrist angle to bring the pads forward and right around the cup without a large joint change, then close.
The cloth bag is nearer the jaws than the target cup. Reopen and shift the low grasp outward toward the cup, changing yaw to avoid the bag.
